newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mixed in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mixed in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trading on Wednesday with many investors remaining sidelined for market-moving news after Tuesday's gains, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 3,386 yuan ($408) per tonne, losing 19 yuan. It opened at 3,390 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 3,415 and a low of 3,384.

May rose 50 to 3,500 yuan per tonne and July 11 to 3,386. November fell six to 3,386 and the January 1998 contract was unchanged at 3,410, the March 1998 contract, traded for the first time, ended at 3,385 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 18,200 tonnes from 25,700 tonnes.
Soybeans opened mixed and moved in a narrow range for most of the session, traders said.
"Most investors are unwilling to enter the market because there is a persistent lack of positive market-moving news," one trader said.
Traders said they expected soybeans to move around the 3,400 yuan level in the short term.
